The polynomial map is trilinear and has zero output coefficient at zero.

The argument explicitly uses polynomial Cauchy approximations and a three-term trilinear difference.

background_notes.justification: Zero coefficient is a continuous functional in each Fourier norm, so mean-zero spaces are closed and mean-zero polynomials are dense there (subtract the approximants' zero coefficients). Approximate each input by such polynomials. A difference of two outputs is a sum of three terms, each having one input difference and two bounded approximating factors; the bound makes outputs Cauchy in the complete mean-zero L2 space. The same estimate proves independence of approximations, passage of the bound and trilinearity. Density gives uniqueness. For s>=0, H^s convergence implies L2 convergence by the weight comparison, so a common polynomial approximation identifies both extensions. The argument requires no convergence of a formal infinite multiplier sum.
